decision.detail: I set the coffee mug down on the marble counter, cap still on, and pick up the camera by the neck strap. The body's warm from sitting in my coat pocket. I unhook it, check the charge light—still one bar, still one shot—and step out the hotel door before anyone can ask if I want another round of pastries. The February air hits my face. The Rialto's marquee is still lit, buzzing, one letter dark. I walk toward it with the camera held at chest height, the way you carry a thing you're about to spend.
decision.intention: Get to the Rialto before the doors lock. Set the camera on the tripod by the booth where Alma sits. Let her talk to the lens the way she'd talk to a projection window. One take. Then wrap the reel, tag it, and get it onto the regional line before the last train out. Pittsburgh by Thursday, maybe earlier if the line's running clean.
decision.words: I don't turn back to the lobby. But I say, low, to the nearest one of them, the one who's still holding a saucer: 'Rialto's closing. I'm going to get a shot before the lights go out. Be back for the party.' It's not a question. I'm already walking.
